india.rationale: Fact: Brent fell to about $93 on Nov 5 (from a peak near $118) on hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic exit after the Democratic midterm sweep, then rebounded to about $98 on Nov 6. NSE provisional data compiled by StockPil show FIIs were net cash-market buyers of Rs 45,960 crore over Nov 2-6, and the October HSBC manufacturing PMI stayed expansionary at 54.7 with output-price inflation at a near four-year low. Interpretation: lower oil and foreign buying (partly a rotation away from AI hardware markets) are a mild tailwind, but the oil relief is fragile (Hormuz attacks continue), and claims that rupee is near 94-95/USD and October CPI near 6% come only from a commercial blog and are unverified. Flow figures are from secondary sources, hence medium confidence.

em_asia_other.rationale: Fact: a global AI and semiconductor rout, tied to fears that the Democratic midterm sweep brings US data-center restrictions, hit Taiwan and Korea hard. KOSPI fell 5.28% on Nov 5 and 6.02% on Nov 6 (circuit breaker triggered, foreign net selling of 2.77tn won, won at 1,356.6). TAIEX fell 3.59% on Nov 3, 3.2% on Nov 5 and 4.51% on Nov 6 to 39,701, with the NT dollar at an 18-month low, a record US$28bn foreign outflow in October, and Taipei ordering the regulator to stabilise the market. Offset: fundamentals remain very strong, with Korea's October exports up 93.7% to a record $115.3bn and chips up 259%. Interpretation: this is a sentiment and flows headwind rather than a demand shock so far; it would move to -2 if US data-center moratoria materialise. ASEAN coverage this week was thin; lower oil is a mild help to importers.

latam.rationale: Fact: Brazil's Copom unanimously held the Selic at 13.75% on Nov 4, ending the easing cycle, and raised its 2026 IPCA projection to 5.6% (above the 4.5% ceiling), warning of de-anchoring expectations and a sharper activity slowdown; Money Times notes the dollar closed at its 2026 high against the real. Banxico cut by 25bp to 6.25% on Nov 5 in a 3-2 split vote, raised its Q4 inflation forecast to 3.7%, and called it a 'one-time adjustment' as the peso has depreciated. Interpretation: stagflation-tinged news in Brazil and a dovish move into currency weakness in Mexico point to a mild headwind for LatAm assets. No in-window Argentina news was found.

em_broad.rationale: Fact: the two largest non-China EM index weights, Taiwan and Korea, suffered multi-day crashes on the AI/semiconductor sell-off with heavy foreign selling and currency weakness. Turkey's October CPI beat forecasts at 29.77% and the lira broke 50/USD to a record low, and the Brazilian real and Mexican peso weakened. Offsetting this, Brent dropped sharply on Iran-diplomacy hopes, which helps oil importers such as India. Interpretation: for a cap-weighted EM basket, the tech-heavy North Asia drawdown outweighs the oil relief, so this is a mild headwind.

regime_notes: The week was dominated by two US-driven shocks that cut opposite ways for EM. First, the Democratic midterm sweep triggered a violent AI and semiconductor sell-off on fears of US data-center restrictions; Korea and Taiwan saw circuit breakers, record foreign outflows, and weaker won and NT dollar, even though Korea's October chip exports hit records. Second, the same result raised hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic exit, so Brent fell from near $118 to about $93 before rebounding to around $98 as Hormuz attacks continued; this favoured oil importers, and India drew strong FII inflows. Elsewhere, Brazil paused at 13.75% with rising inflation projections, Banxico cut to 6.25% despite peso weakness, and Turkey's inflation surprise pushed the lira past 50/USD. The key swing factors for the next 1-3 months are whether US data-center moratoria actually materialise and whether the Iran talks hold. Caveat: in-window coverage of ASEAN, South Africa and Argentina was thin, and the search budget ran out before they could be covered.

red_flags.issue: TAIEX fell up to 9% intraday on Nov 6 and Taipei ordered the FSC to stabilise markets (Taipei Times reports the NT$500bn National Stabilization Fund was authorised). Possible trading-measure changes and wide NAV premium/discount for US-listed Taiwan ETFs; record US$28bn October foreign outflow.

KOSPI circuit breaker and sell-sidecar triggered on Nov 6 (intraday low -8.78%). There is a risk of NAV/price dislocation for US-listed Korea ETFs, and high concentration in Samsung and SK hynix (-6.35% and -10.44% that day).
The lira hit a record low past 50/USD after an October CPI upside surprise; currency-translation losses for USD-based holders.
